title: Silver Reutilization and Account Maintenance Service
description: The Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Keyport is issuing this Request for Quote for Silver Reutilization and Account Maintenance Services. The requirement involves the refinement of silver-bearing material recovered from batteries, for which the refined silver will be used to manufacture new batteries that require silver of 99.9% purity. AnnuaI requirements: Silver Reutilization High Silver Content 380,000 troy ounces | Silver Reutilization Low Silver Content 725,000 troy ounces | Silver Account Maintenance 500,000 troy ounces | Transaction Fee 10 each | Contract Data Requirements List 1 Lot (Not Separately Priced). This Request for Quote is for commercial services and is posted in accordance with FAR Subpart 5.201. The Government intends to award one (1) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a five-year ordering period, using Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) source selection procedures. The contract type will be Firm-Fixed-Price and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment-Cost Index in accordance with FAR 16.203-4(d). The applicable Product Service Code (PSC) for the requirement is P999 (Salvage - other) and the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 331492 (Secondary Smelting, Refining, and Alloying of nonferrous Metal (except Copper and Aluminum)), with a small business size standard of 850 employees. The Request for Quote is competed using full and open competition simplified procedures under FAR Subpart 12.201. The Request for Quote is available through the Solicitation Module in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) at https://piee.eb.mil/. Interested vendors must establish a PIEE account and obtain Proposal Manager role activation through the PIEE Contractor Administrator to submit offers electronically. Vendors will need a Digital PIN, One-Time Password, and CAGE Code to successfully save and submit offers through the system. For information and instructions regarding the Solicitation Module in PIEE, please visit https://dodprocurementtoolbox.com/site-pages/solicitation-module.Offerors must have a current registration and completed representations and certifications in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://sam.gov/, a Federal Government owned website. title: NETSAFA International Training Center Support
description: Amendment released on 11/4/2026 for Volume 1 Q&A responses. The Naval Education and Training Security Assistance Field Activity (NETSAFA), Pensacola, Florida, requires educational and training services, engineering and technical services, logistics, administration, management assistance, consulting and facilitation services, and transportation support services, training liaison, special mission personnel, and curriculum development. These services may be required in various locations in the U.S. or in foreign countries and may include support to foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs) under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP)/Security Assistance Training Program (SATP). The PSC code for this action is U099 Education/Training-Other associated with NAICS code 541330 under the Knowledge Based Services Taxonomy of services. NETSAFA supports international training in all warfare areas and at all levels of training for foreign countries. This is accomplished by staffing, operating, and managing international training support provided at NETSAFAs international training sites. The training sites are located in the NETASAFA International Training Center (NITC) located at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida and NAS Whiting Field, Milton, Florida, and NITC Detachment Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. These sites are outfitted with computer training facilities, classrooms, and equipment needed to teach courses. They provide training and training support services in Navy activities such as government-owned contractor operating facilities. NETSAFAs international training sites are currently operational and have established curriculum. The training and other services required by this Performance Work Statement (PWS) are currently centered in four categories: General Training Programs, Aviation Training Programs, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs). Additionally, support will be required to meet emerging requirements in support of the SCETP/SATP. The instant requirement is for services associated with the international requirement of the United States and the foreign countries participating in the SCETP/SATP for a 12-month base period of performance beginning 01 March 2027 through 29 February 2028, with four (4) consecutive 12-month option periods pursuant to FAR 52.217-9, and a 6-month option period pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The contractor will be required to periodically perform these services in various locations in the U.S. and may be required to perform these services in foreign countries. If support is needed in a foreign country, the contractor may be required to support foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, mobile training teams, and mobile education teams under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP) /Security Assistance Training Program (SATP).

title: Overhaul of the UH-60 POWER TURBINE MODULE
description: The purpose of this Amendment 0004 to solicitation W58RGZ-26-B-0012 is to formally update the acquisition approach and restructure the requirement. The Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Commercial Item Group (CIG) has issued a formal determination concluding that the maintenance and overhaul (M&O) services for the Power Turbine Module of the Black Hawk weapons system described in this solicitation meet the definition of a commercial product/commercial service in accordance with FAR 2.101. Consequently, this solicitation is hereby converted from a noncommercial requirement to a commercial requirement conducted under FAR Part 12. Additionally, this amendment restructures the contract type from a five-year Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to a three-year IDIQ and incorporates mandatory regulatory updates in compliance with the recent Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO).

title: Long-Term Storage and Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Services for Government-Owned Microelectronics
description: 1. Scope of Requirement DLA Weapons Support is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing comprehensive Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) storage, management, packaging, and distribution (including packaging and shipping to third party integrator) for Government-Owned, serialized microcircuits. Management of inventory includes execution of full suite of Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) ANSI X.12 transactions and maintenance of data in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE), including the Government Furnished Property (GFP) Module and/or Item Unique Identification (IUID) Registry. Management also includes delivering Contract Data Requirement List items such as annual inventory reports and inventory management plans. All hardware to be stored and managed is 100% manufactured and has been inspected, accepted, and is owned by the Government. The contemplated effort is strictly for logistics and warehousing services; no manufacturing, specialized electrical acceptance testing, or original design technical data packages (TDPs) are involved. DLA is contemplating firm fixed price contracts with a one year base period and up to eight one-year option periods. Beginning date for base period is TBD, and contract price structure is subject to change. 2. Key Technical & Operational Requirements Vendor Managed Inventory service includes, but is not limited to, entering the Government property into the Contractor�s inventory management system; storing these items in a secure location to prevent their accidental loss, theft, or tampering; transferring these items from inventory to fill authorized requests, and generating the necessary inventory reports in accordance with established DLA VMI practices. Delivery of an inventory management plan in accordance with FAR 52.245-1, to include quality control, subject to approval by DLA. Inventory plan and management system must be capable of accounting for assets by serial number or unique item identifier (UII, as defined by DFARS 252.211-7003) from acceptance to transfer to using entity. Capability to maintain, monitor, and certify long-term storage environments within contractor owned facility until material is transferred out of VMI. Storage must be specifically designed to prevent oxidation and moisture-induced degradation of microcircuits in accordance with GEIA-STD-0003A. Storage duration is to be determined. Requirement may include packaging, handling, and transportation for shipments to the next higher assembly (NHA) integrator. Upon authorized release and removal from inventory, the contractor would be required to prepare, package, and transport microcircuits IAW MIL-STD-2073/1, and MIL-STD-129. Capability to establish, test, and maintain production Defense Logistics Management Standards (DLMS) EDI transaction feeds per DLA EDI Onboarding Guide Generate reconciliation reports at the end of each month for NIINs in inventory to determine the physical inventory remaining at the Contractor�s location. This inventory record would be generated using Contractor�s inventory management system. Provide inventory detail reports, balances, and transaction history to support requests from external and internal auditors. Perform annual audits in coordination with DLA and in accordance with DLAI 4000.02, DLA Annual Physical Inventory Control Program (PICP) for Non-Energy WCF Material (Enclosure 4), and submit required documentation as defined therein. Additional support required for all Government audits, including providing access to Contractor facilities used in the execution of this contract, providing information pertaining to execution of contract objectives and tasks, and supporting meeting requests during audit execution and any audit report reviews. Capability to dispose of all unusable inventory in accordance with CNSSI 3006 upon notification by the Government. 3. Capability Statement Questionnaire (Requested Industry Input) Interested parties are requested to submit a brief Capability Statement (maximum 5�10 pages) addressing the following criteria: Company & Business Profile: Company Name, CAGE Code, UEI, Point of Contact information. Business Size Status under NAICS 493190 (Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, or Large Business). Technical & Storage Experience: Describe your facility�s capabilities and past performance in executing long-term storage of sensitive microelectronics under GEIA-STD-0003A and ANSI/ESD S20.20. Outline your environmental monitoring systems (temperature, relative humidity, nitrogen purge/dry box controls) and contingency backup protocols. Describe your company�s experience/ability to handle and package microelectronics. Systems Integration & EDI Capabilities: Detail your experience integrating internal Warehouse Management Systems (WMS) with DoD/DLA systems via DLMS/EDI ANSI X.12. Estimate the standard timeline required for your firm to complete end-to-end EDI ANSI X.12 onboarding and validation testing with DLA Transaction Services. Government Property & Inventory Controls: Describe your approved Government Property Management System compliance with DFARS 252.245-7005 and FAR 52.245-1. Outline your process for conducting annual 100% wall-to-wall physical inventories and handling Supply Discrepancy Reporting (SDR) Product Quality Deficiency Report (PQDR) quarantine staging per DLAI 4000.03. Security & Facility Controls: Confirm facility security measures and capability to securely store and handle Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and mission-critical hardware. Contract Pricing: DLA is open to alternative pricing arrangements (e.g., hybrid FFP/Transactional or Time-and-Materials for logistics services). Please briefly describe the pricing structure your firm typically uses to optimize cost efficiency and predictability for this scope of work. Cost Accounting System: Indicate whether your firm possesses a Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) approved cost accounting system. If approved, provide the date of the last audit and the cognizant DCAA office. Forward Pricing Rates: Confirm whether your firm has established Forward Pricing Rate Agreements (FPRAs) or Forward Pricing Rate Recommendations (FPRRs) with DCAA/DCMA. If so, specify the validity period. 4. Applicable Reference Documents & Access Instructions To assist industry in preparing responses to this notice, the Government is referencing the following standards and documents. DLA Transaction Services EDI Onboarding Guide: Attached directly to this SAM.gov announcement. DLAI 4000.02 is available at https://dlamil.dps.mil/sites/DLA_Issuances. DLAI 4000.03: Interested vendors may request a copy of these issuances by contacting ryan.collier@dla.mil Military Standards: The following public military standards apply to this requirement and are available online via the Defense Logistics Agency and Assist Quick Search databases (https://quicksearch.dla.mil/): MIL-STD-2073-1 � Standard Practice for Military Packaging MIL-STD-129 � Military Marking for Shipment and Storage GEIA-STD-0003A (Standard for Long-Term Storage of Microcircuit Packages): Notice: This is a copyrighted, commercially licensed standard published by SAE International. The Government will not provide copies of this document. How to Obtain: Interested parties must obtain their own copy of this standard through authorized commercial distributors, such as SAE International (https://www.sae.org) or IHS Markit. Compliance with this standard is a mandatory threshold requirement for contract performance. The information gathered from this announcement will be used to determine if responsible sources exist and to assist in determining if this effort can be competitive. title: Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC)
description: This is a Sources Sought/Request for Information (RFI) in attempt to determine local vendor capability/identify potential sources at Joint Base Anacostia Bolling (JBAB), DC 20032 and Andrews AFB, MD 20762 in accordance with RFO Part 10, Market Research. PLEASE NOTE - No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this synopsis or any follow up information requests. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. The purpose of this Sources Sought/RFI is to conduct market research for planning purposes to determine if responsible sources exist and to assist in determining if future efforts can be solicited on a competitive basis. This sources sought/RFI is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Description The 11th Contracting Squadron is publicizing this SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE in order to gather industry interest and information with respect to a potential Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Design-Build, Progressive Design-Build, Accelerated Design-Build, Design-Bid-Build Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) program. The government is seeking to identify qualified, experienced, and interested potential businesses capable of performing the type of work as described herein. The MACC provides a vehicle for execution of a broad range of maintenance; repair and minor/complex construction. For the purpose of this Request for Information (RFI), the work to be performed under the MACC will be within the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) codes as follows: 236210 ($45M Size Standard). Contractors will be expected to accomplish a wide variety of individual construction projects, including design/progressive design build (ranging from concept up to full 100% design), renovation, and additions/upgrades, along with specific work in hazardous material survey/abatement, heating/ventilation/air conditioning, electrical, mechanical, and other major trades. In-house design capability or ready access to design capability is a must for projects under the MACC. Description of the work will be identified in each individual task order. Individual task orders may range from $350,000 to $50,000,000. The program value is Not-to-Exceed $900,000,000 over a ten-year period. This acquisition is being considered as a 100% competitive 8(a) set-aside. All interested parties are invited to respond and prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at http://www.sam/gov/ before award of a government contract; failure to register in the SAM database will cause your firm to be ineligible for any future award. Any subsequent RFP will include a seed project that will be used to rate offeror's capabilities to determine basic contract awardees. The highest rated awardee will also receive award of the seed project. All other successful contract awardees are guaranteed a minimum of $2,500 during the first task order only. The government will compete future individual requirements with all of the awardees. The government anticipates an award of up to ten (10) contracts. The government will evaluate offers utilizing the best value source selection procedures described in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (RFO FAR Part 15), Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS 215), and DoD Source Selection Procedures. If your firm has an interest in proposing on a future requirement as described above, please prepare a Capability Statement with details as follows: 1. Company name, address, point of contact (POC), telephone and email address of POC, CAGE Code, DUNS number. 2. Company's business size, to include the number of employees, number of years in the construction industry, and average annual gross revenue for the last three fiscal years. 3. Socioeconomic status, (e.g., SBA Certified 8(a) Program Participant). 4. Potential teaming arrangements and delineation between the work that will be accomplished by the prime and the work accomplished by the teaming partner(s). Note: For general and heavy construction 15% of the cost of the contract, not including the cost of materials, must be performed by the prime contractor with its own employees. 5. Representation of ability to execute a broad range of maintenance, repair, and construction of real property (i.e. carpentry, excavation, interior renovation, exterior renovation, electrical, plumbing, painting, paving, roofing, demolition, masonry, hazardous material survey/abatement, and HVAC) from an on-the-shelf design, or a design provided in-house or through subcontract designers (including design ranging from concept to full 100% design). Identify specialty construction trades performed by prime company employees, if any, as well as experience in delivering multi-trade design/build projects. 6. In-house Architect-Engineering capability, up to complete 100% design or ready access to design capability. Identify if you : 1) have in-house design capability; 2) have state certified Professional Engineers and/or registered Architects on staff ; 3) which A-E disciplines you have the ability to design in-house (Mechanical, Electrical, Structural, Fire Protection, etc.), and 4) or whether you subcontract all A-E services. 7. Surge capability to provide significant increase in support (e.g. rapidly identify, employ and equip resources) in the event of a government End of Fiscal Year (EOFY) or Economic surge in number, size or complexity of projects. 8. Past/Current performance for projects within the last 3 years where your firm was the Prime Contractor, to include: a. Contract identification number(s) b. Title and a brief summary of the project requirements c. Contracting Agency or firm (Government or commercial) d. Value of contracts at award and completion to include the number/value of modifications e. Type of contract (fixed price, cost reimbursement, labor hour, etc.) f. Design-Build or Bid-Build (looking for representation of each) g. Percentage of work done as the Prime Contractor 9. Largest multi-trade project your company has successfully completed, to include value, name and location of client, date completed, and whether the project was renovation or new construction. 10. Identify bonding capacity and name(s) of surety(ies). 11. Provide recommendations of commercial practices the Government should consider implementing for this acquisition.

title: NETSAFA International Training Center Support
description: The Naval Education and Training Security Assistance Field Activity (NETSAFA), Pensacola, Florida, requires educational and training services, engineering and technical services, logistics, administration, management assistance, consulting and facilitation services, and transportation support services, training liaison, special mission personnel, and curriculum development. These services may be required in various locations in the U.S. or in foreign countries and may include support to foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs) under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP)/Security Assistance Training Program (SATP). The PSC code for this action is U099 Education/Training-Other associated with NAICS code 541330 under the Knowledge Based Services Taxonomy of services. NETSAFA supports international training in all warfare areas and at all levels of training for foreign countries. This is accomplished by staffing, operating, and managing international training support provided at NETSAFAs international training sites. The training sites are located in the NETASAFA International Training Center (NITC) located at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida and NAS Whiting Field, Milton, Florida, and NITC Detachment Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. These sites are outfitted with computer training facilities, classrooms, and equipment needed to teach courses. They provide training and training support services in Navy activities such as government-owned contractor operating facilities. NETSAFAs international training sites are currently operational and have established curriculum. The training and other services required by this Performance Work Statement (PWS) are currently centered in four categories: General Training Programs, Aviation Training Programs, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs). Additionally, support will be required to meet emerging requirements in support of the SCETP/SATP. The instant requirement is for services associated with the international requirement of the United States and the foreign countries participating in the SCETP/SATP for a 12-month base period of performance beginning 01 March 2027 through 29 February 2028, with four (4) consecutive 12-month option periods pursuant to FAR 52.217-9, and a 6-month option period pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The contractor will be required to periodically perform these services in various locations in the U.S. and may be required to perform these services in foreign countries. If support is needed in a foreign country, the contractor may be required to support foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, mobile training teams, and mobile education teams under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP) /Security Assistance Training Program (SATP).

title: Silver Reutilization and Account Maintenance Service
description: The Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Keyport is issuing this Request for Quote for Silver Reutilization and Account Maintenance Services. The requirement involves the refinement of silver-bearing material recovered from batteries, for which the refined silver will be used to manufacture new batteries that require silver of 99.9% purity. This Request for Quote is for commercial services and is posted in accordance with FAR Subpart 5.201. The Government intends to award one (1) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a five-year ordering period, using Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) source selection procedures. The Request for Quote is competed using full and open competition simplified procedures under FAR Subpart 12.201. title: Army Enterprise HVAC Modernization and Lifecycle Sustainment Maintenance
description: ***************START OF 06 NOV UPDATE*************** A CSO Question & Answer (Q&A) file is attached herein to provide government responses/clarity to all interested parties. Additionally, CSO Amendment 0002 (A002) has been issued/posted herein to clarify requirements at para. 3.2.1 and to require MICC POC be placed on copy when industry questions are submitted to the AoI POC. The Phase 1 response date remains unchanged, 30 Nov 2026, 4:30PM EST. ***************END OF 06 NOV UPDATE****************** ***************START OF 02 NOV UPDATE*************** CSO Amendment 0001 (A001), to provide the incorporated Attachment 3, is posted herein. The Phase 1 response date remains unchanged, 30 Nov 2026, 4:30PM EST. ***************END OF 02 NOV UPDATE****************** The U.S. Army Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC), on behalf of the U.S. Army Installation Management Command (IMCOM), is seeking innovative commercial technologies, products and/or services that will provide an Army Enterprise Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) Modernization & Lifecycle Sustainment Maintenance Plan, and associated project management of the plan throughout the project period, Fiscal Year (FY) FY27-FY31. This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) will utilize a solicitation process authorized by Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) DFARS Subpart 212.70. Under this CSO, the Department of War (DoW) will be allowed to competitively procure innovative commercial technologies, products and/or services that will provide a solution for Army Enterprise HVAC modernization and lifecycle sustainment maintenance. CSO procedures provide a streamlined acquisition process and simplified contract terms resulting in RFO FAR-based contracts awarded under RFO FAR Part 12 Commercial Item Procedures. Both traditional and non-traditional defense contractors may be awarded contracts under this CSO. Under a CSO DoW contracting (or agreement) officers may competitively select proposals received in response to a general competitive solicitation, similar to a broad agency announcement, based on a review of proposals by scientific, technological, or other subject matter experts. While this is a complete CSO as detailed herein, the MICC reserves the right to pursue alternative contracting methods as a result of Offeror responses to Phase 1 requirements herein and continued government analysis. For example, the government may elect to pursue a solution via Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). If this, or any other change occurs, the public will be notified via sam.gov posting. Industry parties interested in responding to this CSO shall request access to Attachments 1 and 2 by submitting justification/reason for access as instructed in this sam.gov post. The MICC team will receive notification of the request, review, and release, as appropriate, within one business day. Finally, the government anticipates hosting a future industry conference. Accordingly, industry is encouraged to monitor this sam.gov posting for updates, to include the date, time, and location of any such event.

title: Germany – Lift installation work – Staatliche Grundschule Niedersalza; Los 07 - Aufzugsanlage
description: Die Stadtverwaltung Nordhausen plant die Durchführung der „Sanierung, Erweiterung und der barrierefreien Erschließung“ am Objekt: Staatliche Grundschule „Niedersalza“ in Nordhausen. Die GS Niedersalza wurde in den 50er Jahren erbaut und ab 2008 in Abschnitten teilsaniert. Es werden hier z. Zt. rd. 160 Schüler unterrichtet. Die Schule ist leergezogen und in einem Ausweichquartier untergebracht. Die hier ausgeschriebene Leistung umfasst das "Los 07 - Aufzugsanlage" (in dieser Bekanntgabe unter Punkt 5 als LOT-0001 geführt). title: Germany – Road transport services – Entsorgungsarbeiten (Teil 3) zur Baumaßnahme "Grundhafter Ausbau der Wallrothstraße, 1. BA"
description: Die im Rahmen der Baumaßnahme "Grundhafter Ausbau der Wallrothstraße, 1. BA" entstandenen Aushub- und Abbruchmaterialien sollen fachgerecht entsorgt bzw. einer Verwertung zugeführt werden. Die Abbruchmaterialien sind derzeit auf einem gut erreichbaren innerstädtischen Lagerplatz zwischengelagert. Die Leistung umfasst das Aufnehmen, Laden, den Transport und die Entsorgung (Verwertung bzw. Beseitigung) von ca. 5.500 t zwischengelagerten Aushub- und Abbruchmaterialien (Boden, Asphaltaufbruch, Betonbruch) aus dem 1. Bauabschnitt des grundhaften Ausbaus der Wallrothstraße, Lagerplatz Beethovenring, Nordhausen, davon ca. 300 t bleibelasteter Boden als gefährlicher Abfall (AVV 17 05 03*) mit Nachweisführung im eANV. Es handelt sich dabei um den 3. Teil der Entsorgungsarbeiten für den 1. Bauabschnitt der Baumaßnahme (in dieser Bekanntgabe unter Punkt 5 als LOT-0001 geführt). Eine Unterteilung der hier ausgeschriebenen Leistungen in weitere Lose ist nicht vorgesehen.

title: Catering Services - Battle Creek ANGB
description: The 110th Wing is conducting preliminary Market Research to assess market availability of vendors who are able to provide Catered Meal Services during regularly scheduled drills (RSD) to Battle Creek Air National Guard Base, Michigan. No solicitation is available at this time. Responses will be used to determine acquisition strategies, evaluate market capabilities, and identify potential sources. If a future award is made, it is expected to result in a Firm-Fixed-Price contract. Requirements: Provide catered box meals for approximately 175 personnel per meal delivered to Battle Creek ANGB. Only one meal per drill weekend is anticipated. Boxed meals are the only anticipated meal type required. Meals will be prepared off-site and delivered to Battle Creek ANGB 30 minutes before the scheduled mealtimes. Please see attached DRAFT Description of Services (DOS) for additional information. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code anticipated for industry classification is 722320, "Caterers." All information from interested parties that is received in response to this Sources Sought notice will be collected and saved until which time this potential requirement becomes defined. A solicitation MAY be issued at that time. This Sources Sought Notice is being posted for Market Research purposes only to identify potential vendors and evaluate Small Business capabilities who are able to provide the supplies listed above and further described in the attached Salient Characteristics. If you are interested providing these services, please provide a capability statement identifying your firm�s ability to meet these requirements via email to MSgt Michael Solo at michael.solo.4@us.af.mil. If have any questions regarding this requirement, please submit as a Request for Information (RFI) to MSgt Michael Solo at the email above. This office may reach out to interested parties who respond to this notice for additional information to further investigate capabilities of meeting the requirement.

title: P-8A OFT Technical Refresh
description: The Department of the Navy, Naval Air Warfare Center Training Systems Division (NAWCTSD), Orlando, FL, seeks potential sources possessing the requisite technical capabilities, expertise, and facilities to execute updates, hardware, and integration services to upgrade the P-8A OFT for the USN. The contemplated effort requires engineering, modernization, and logistics support for a Tech Refresh effort on the P-8A OFTs at Naval Air Station (NAS) Jacksonville (JAX) (10 OFTs), NAS Whidbey Island (WHI) (7 OFTs) and the System Development and Demonstration (SDD) Lab in St. Louis (1 OFT). See attached Sources Sought Notice.

title: Project Manager Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) Virtual Industry Day - Q&A RESPONSES INCLUDED
description: ** THIS INDUSTRY DAY HAS ALREADY OCCURED. Once your registration is received, you will be provided with the MS Teams Live link. Registration Link: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/cphuQr7k47

title: GSA PBS National Multiple Award IDIQ for Fine Arts, Architectural Arts and Decorative Arts Services - Sources Sought Notice
description: GSA PBS National Multiple Award IDIQ for Fine Arts, Architectural Arts and Decorative Arts Services This is a Sources Sought Notice and is for informational purposes only. NO AWARD WILL BE GENERATED FROM THIS NOTICE.THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS, QUOTATIONS, OR BIDS. Per Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responses do not affect a potential offeror's ability to respond to any future synopsis/solicitation. This announcement is a market survey for information only. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. A solicitation does not presently exist. Respondents will not be notified of the evaluation and any information by respondents to this notice is strictly voluntary. This sources sought synopsis is for an Nationwide Fine Art Services Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract. The primary use of this contract will be for Fine Art Assessment, Conservation, and Maintenance Services of Paintings, Photographs, Prints, Textiles, Sculptures, Time-Based Media, Architectural and Decorative Arts, as well as Architectural and Materials Conservation for the United States and all U.S. Territories. The U. S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), Indefinite Delivery Vehicle Branch (PQ1AA) is conducting market research to determine if there are adequate Small Business contractors who are technically capable of performing services for the anticipated solicitation for a National Fine Art Services Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity Contract. Description of Intended Contract An IDIQ is a type of contract that provides for an indefinite quantity, within stated limits, of supplies or services during a fixed period. GSA intends to award multiple contracts for fine arts and architectural conservation services resulting from a future solicitation. The number of awardees will be determined at a later date. Awardees will be provided fair opportunity in accordance with FAR 16.507 for specific requirements where a single task order will be issued based on selection criteria established at the ordering level, unless an exemption exists. These IDIQ contracts may be made available for use to any Federal agency with the appropriate contracting authority to be able to place task orders against Government-wide IDIQ contracts. Industry feedback on this approach is also requested. Each contract awarded will contain a guaranteed minimum amount for the base period to be identified in the solicitation. The Multiple Award IDIQ will be for a maximum contract length of five years. The first ordering period is expected to begin in Spring 2027. General Description of Services The Contractor shall furnish the necessary materials, skilled labor, supplies and management to provide industry standard fine arts and architectural/material conservation and repair services, which include, but are not limited to, surveys, assessments, scientific analysis, treatment recommendations, transportation, conservation treatment services, cleaning, emergency stabilization/repair, architectural materials treatment and repairs to include masonry, metal and wood finishes, and the development and enactment of artwork cyclic maintenance plans. The contractor may be required to respond to a variety of fine arts requests within a limited time frame and provide project coordination. The following tasks are anticipated: On Site Examination of Artwork Condition Assessment and Treatment Recommendation Report which may require archival research and non-destructive laboratory analyses. Performance of Conservation Treatment including a written report detailing final testing, treatment(s), remedial materials and methods, and specific recommendations for future cyclic care and maintenance. Performance of Architectural Materials Conservation and Repairs including a written report detailing final testing, treatment(s), remedial materials and methods, and specific recommendations for future cyclic care and maintenance. Artwork Protection for example during construction, renovation, or modernization projects. Emergency Response, which may include stabilization, damage mitigation, and/or disaster mitigation. Education and Training Cyclic Maintenance including development of maintenance plans and performance of the maintenance. Location of Services GSA anticipates awarding multiple contracts on a nationwide basis. The Government is also considering alternatively structuring the IDIQ contracts on a zonal basis. The zones would be organized in a geographic pattern as follows: Zone 1 - Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, Washington, DC, West Virginia Zone 2 - Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, Vermont, Virgin Islands Zone 3 - Alabama, Florida, Georgia Zone 4 - Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Tennessee, Wisconsin Zone 5 - Arkansas, Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Utah, Wyoming Zone 6 - Louisiana, Texas, Mississippi Zone 7 - American Samoa, Alaska, Arizona, California, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Northern Marianas, Oregon, Saipan, Washington Please indicate whether you are interested in one or more geographic zones on the sources sought questionnaire. Industry feedback on this approach is also requested. Size Standard GSA anticipates soliciting this procurement under one or more NAICS codes. Currently, the anticipated NAICS codes and size standards are: NAICS 711510, Independent Artists, Writers, and Performers, the small business size standard is $9 million. NAICS 541990, All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services, the small business size standard is $19.5 million. Selection Procedures The anticipated contract will be procured utilizing one of the source selection procedures as described in FAR Part 15.103 to select the firms offering the best value to the Government. Insurance Firms will be expected to provide and maintain, during the entire performance of the contract, the minimum amounts of insurance required for work on a Government Installation, in accordance with FAR Clause 52.228-5. The minimum amounts, as specified in FAR subpart 28.307-2, are as follows: Workers Compensation and Employer�s Liability ($100,000); General Liability ($500,000 per occurrence / $50,000 per occurrence for property damage); Automobile Liability ($200,000 per person / $500,000 per occurrence for bodily injury / $20,000 per occurrence for property damage). System for Award Management Registration All contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database. The website for registration in the SAM database is www.sam.gov. All contractors interested in obtaining a copy of the anticipated future solicitation must be registered in the Government Point of Entry (GPE) � www.sam.gov. If a contractor is unable to complete this form through the Google suite, they shall complete the attached form and return to the contracting officer no later than 5:00 PM EDT on Wednesday, November 25, 2026 via email to tracy.comose@gsa.gov. Responses to this sources sought announcement will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. All interested Small Business contractors are encouraged to submit responses. title: AFLCMC Cloud Productivity Suite Pilot CSO
description: The AFLCMC Cloud Productivity Suite Pilot (CPSP) Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) seeks white paper submittals from vendors which detail their approach to providing an integrated productivity suite/cloud tenant/operating system offering to the DAF IT enterprise, including providing alternative services and integrations for productivity suites. This is a competitive solicitation posted on this Government Point of Entry (GPE) www.sam.gov through November 2026. The CSO authority is 10 U.S.C. 3458, implemented by DFARS Subpart 212.70, for the acquisition of innovative commercial products or commercial services. Per 10 U.S.C. 3458, innovative products/services competitively selected by peer review of proposals resulting from a general solicitation (e.g., this CTP CSO) are considered commercial notwithstanding the de?nition under FAR Subpart 2.101. The use of a CSO is permanently authorized by section 803 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2022 (Pub. L. 117-81) codi?ed at 10 U.S.C 3458. The DAF Enterprise IT branch is interested in innovative technologies and services related to the areas of interest listed below. Submissions should identify innovative solutions that fill capability needs related to secure cloud instances, a comprehensive productivity suite, and hardware solutions like laptops that support seamless integration for DAF-wide adoption. This is essential to ensure that all Air Force personnel have access to reliable, secure, and efficient IT tools that meet their unique operational needs. The level of detail provided for each topic or the order in which they appear is not intended to convey any information regarding relative priority. There are no specific Technology Readiness Level (TRL) requirements for proposed projects. However, proposed prototypes or solutions should be at a high enough TRL to enable the assessment of the viability, technical feasibility, application, or military utility of the proposed solution and support a rapid transition into operations and scaling to the DAF. The end prototype or solution must be Impact Level 5 (IL5) approved by the end of this effort at minimum. The Government reserves the right to fund all, some, one or none of the proposals submitted; may elect to fund only part of a submitted proposal; and may incrementally fund any or all awards under this CSO. All awards are subject to the availability of funds. See the attached AFLCMC CPSP CSO with Attachment 1, Submittal Instructions for full details and additional instructions.

title: AFLCMC Cloud Productivity Suite Pilot CSO
description: The AFLCMC Cloud Productivity Suite Pilot (CPSP) Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) seeks white paper submittals from vendors which detail their approach to providing an integrated productivity suite/cloud tenant/operating system offering to the DAF IT enterprise, including providing alternative services and integrations for productivity suites. This is a competitive solicitation posted on this Government Point of Entry (GPE) www.sam.gov through November 2026. The CSO authority is 10 U.S.C. 3458, implemented by DFARS Subpart 212.70, for the acquisition of innovative commercial products or commercial services. Per 10 U.S.C. 3458, innovative products/services competitively selected by peer review of proposals resulting from a general solicitation (e.g., this CTP CSO) are considered commercial notwithstanding the de?nition under FAR Subpart 2.101. The use of a CSO is permanently authorized by section 803 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2022 (Pub. L. 117-81) codi?ed at 10 U.S.C 3458. The DAF Enterprise IT branch is interested in innovative technologies and services related to the areas of interest listed below. Submissions should identify innovative solutions that fill capability needs related to secure cloud instances, a comprehensive productivity suite, and hardware solutions like laptops that support seamless integration for DAF-wide adoption. This is essential to ensure that all Air Force personnel have access to reliable, secure, and efficient IT tools that meet their unique operational needs. The level of detail provided for each topic or the order in which they appear is not intended to convey any information regarding relative priority. There are no specific Technology Readiness Level (TRL) requirements for proposed projects. However, proposed prototypes or solutions should be at a high enough TRL to enable the assessment of the viability, technical feasibility, application, or military utility of the proposed solution and support a rapid transition into operations and scaling to the DAF. The end prototype or solution must be Impact Level 5 (IL5) approved by the end of this effort at minimum. The Government reserves the right to fund all, some, one or none of the proposals submitted; may elect to fund only part of a submitted proposal; and may incrementally fund any or all awards under this CSO. All awards are subject to the availability of funds. See the attached AFLCMC CPSP CSO with Attachment 1, Submittal Instructions for full details and additional instructions.

title: GSA PBS National Multiple Award IDIQ for Fine Arts, Architectural Arts and Decorative Arts Conservation Services - Sources Sought Notice
description: GSA PBS National Multiple Award IDIQ for Fine Arts, Architectural Arts and Decorative Arts Services This is a Sources Sought Notice and is for informational purposes only. NO AWARD WILL BE GENERATED FROM THIS NOTICE.THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS, QUOTATIONS, OR BIDS. Per Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responses do not affect a potential offeror's ability to respond to any future synopsis/solicitation. This announcement is a market survey for information only. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. A solicitation does not presently exist. Respondents will not be notified of the evaluation and any information by respondents to this notice is strictly voluntary. This sources sought synopsis is for an Nationwide Fine Art Services Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract. The primary use of this contract will be for Fine Art Assessment, Conservation, and Maintenance Services of Paintings, Photographs, Prints, Textiles, Sculptures, Time-Based Media, Architectural and Decorative Arts, as well as Architectural and Materials Conservation for the United States and all U.S. Territories. The U. S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), Indefinite Delivery Vehicle Branch (PQ1AA) is conducting market research to determine if there are adequate Small Business contractors who are technically capable of performing services for the anticipated solicitation for a National Fine Art Services Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity Contract. Description of Intended Contract An IDIQ is a type of contract that provides for an indefinite quantity, within stated limits, of supplies or services during a fixed period. GSA intends to award multiple contracts for fine arts and architectural conservation services resulting from a future solicitation. The number of awardees will be determined at a later date. Awardees will be provided fair opportunity in accordance with FAR 16.507 for specific requirements where a single task order will be issued based on selection criteria established at the ordering level, unless an exemption exists. These IDIQ contracts may be made available for use to any Federal agency with the appropriate contracting authority to be able to place task orders against Government-wide IDIQ contracts. Industry feedback on this approach is also requested. Each contract awarded will contain a guaranteed minimum amount for the base period to be identified in the solicitation. The Multiple Award IDIQ will be for a maximum contract length of five years. The first ordering period is expected to begin in Spring 2027. General Description of Services The Contractor shall furnish the necessary materials, skilled labor, supplies and management to provide industry standard fine arts and architectural/material conservation and repair services, which include, but are not limited to, surveys, assessments, scientific analysis, treatment recommendations, transportation, conservation treatment services, cleaning, emergency stabilization/repair, architectural materials treatment and repairs to include masonry, metal and wood finishes, and the development and enactment of artwork cyclic maintenance plans. The contractor may be required to respond to a variety of fine arts requests within a limited time frame and provide project coordination. The following tasks are anticipated: On Site Examination of Artwork Condition Assessment and Treatment Recommendation Report which may require archival research and non-destructive laboratory analyses. Performance of Conservation Treatment including a written report detailing final testing, treatment(s), remedial materials and methods, and specific recommendations for future cyclic care and maintenance. Performance of Architectural Materials Conservation and Repairs including a written report detailing final testing, treatment(s), remedial materials and methods, and specific recommendations for future cyclic care and maintenance. Artwork Protection for example during construction, renovation, or modernization projects. Emergency Response, which may include stabilization, damage mitigation, and/or disaster mitigation. Education and Training Cyclic Maintenance including development of maintenance plans and performance of the maintenance. Location of Services GSA anticipates awarding multiple contracts on a nationwide basis. The Government is also considering alternatively structuring the IDIQ contracts on a zonal basis. The zones would be organized in a geographic pattern as follows: Zone 1 - Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, Washington, DC, West Virginia Zone 2 - Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, Vermont, Virgin Islands Zone 3 - Alabama, Florida, Georgia Zone 4 - Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Tennessee, Wisconsin Zone 5 - Arkansas, Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Utah, Wyoming Zone 6 - Louisiana, Texas, Mississippi Zone 7 - American Samoa, Alaska, Arizona, California, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Northern Marianas, Oregon, Saipan, Washington Please indicate whether you are interested in one or more geographic zones on the sources sought questionnaire. Industry feedback on this approach is also requested. Size Standard GSA anticipates soliciting this procurement under one or more NAICS codes. Currently, the anticipated NAICS codes and size standards are: NAICS 711510, Independent Artists, Writers, and Performers, the small business size standard is $9 million. NAICS 541990, All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services, the small business size standard is $19.5 million. Selection Procedures The anticipated contract will be procured utilizing one of the source selection procedures as described in FAR Part 15.103 to select the firms offering the best value to the Government. Insurance Firms will be expected to provide and maintain, during the entire performance of the contract, the minimum amounts of insurance required for work on a Government Installation, in accordance with FAR Clause 52.228-5. The minimum amounts, as specified in FAR subpart 28.307-2, are as follows: Workers Compensation and Employer�s Liability ($100,000); General Liability ($500,000 per occurrence / $50,000 per occurrence for property damage); Automobile Liability ($200,000 per person / $500,000 per occurrence for bodily injury / $20,000 per occurrence for property damage). title: Kantonsschulen Rämibühl | Gesamtinstandsetzung | Kunst und Bau
description:
The Building Department of the Canton of Zurich is organising a study commission through a selective procedure for an artistic intervention at the Rämibühl Cantonal Schools as part of their refurbishment. The institutions using the premises are the Realgymnasium Rämibühl (RG) and the Mathematisch-Naturwissenschaftliches Gymnasium Rämibühl (MNG). The client is the Canton of Zurich. Overall responsibility and project management lie with the Building Department of the Canton of Zurich (HBA). The general planning consultant is BS+EMI AG, Zurich. Landscape architecture is the responsibility of mavo Landschaften GmbH, Zurich.


The study commission for the Rämibühl Cantonal Schools aims to identify an artistic intervention in the interior and/or exterior spaces that engages in a stimulating dialogue with the architecture and the site's function as an open environment for teaching and learning, thereby bringing architecture and art together into a cohesive overall concept.


The jury will assess the submitted projects based on their relevance to the Rämibühl Cantonal Schools as a place of education and everyday life, their engagement with the brief and the specific qualities of the site, their artistic merit, and their interaction with the architecture and the function of the complex as a whole. An in-depth engagement with Eduard Neuenschwander's design as an integrated work encompassing landscape, architecture and art is expected, taking into account its heritage significance and its use as a school. The artistic proposals should demonstrate a distinctive and compelling visual language.

buyer: Office fédéral des routes (OFROU), Division Infrastructure routière Est, F3 Filiale de Zofingue
title: MP-250014, Système de drainage de Beckenried Ischenstollen, remplacement du filtre de drainage Travaux de construction
description:
Dans le secteur d’Ischenwald, au-dessus d’Emmetten, se trouve une importante masse sujette au glissement. Pour atténuer l’activité du glissement et les laves torrentielles sur la face avant de la masse, la galerie Ischenstollen a été creusée à la fin des années 1970, puis étendue à la fin des années 1980. À partir de la galerie, des filtres de drainage dont la longueur peut atteindre jusqu’à 50 m traversent les couches de matériaux meubles et le plan de glissement, afin de drainer ce dernier.

À l’heure actuelle, la surface de glissement se déplace à raison d’env. 20 mm/an. Le débit journalier moyen varie, selon la période de l’année, entre 10 et 80 m/s.

Lors d’un glissement de terrain en 1999, presque toutes les crépines ont été endommagées par le cisaillement. Elles ont été remplacées dans les années 2000-2001. Depuis lors, de nombreux tubes perforés ont été écrasés ou endommagés par le cisaillement dans le secteur du plan de glissement. La capacité de drainage ne s’en trouve certes pas encore affectée, mais elle devrait diminuer ces prochaines années.

Le projet de construction comprend le remplacement de tous les filtres de drainage dans la galerie principale et l’extension ; les filtres existants continuent à être exploités.

Les forages pour les filtres doivent être effectués dans la galerie étroite, entre les tubes existants, en procédant du bas vers le haut (15 à 35 degrés à partir de la verticale).

Des travaux de réfection du béton sont en outre prévus au niveau de la voûte et du parement ainsi que du lit, de même que des travaux sur les tubes existants. L’eau de ruissellement et les eaux chargées doivent être captées, analysées et traitées séparément.


Valeurs principales :

Travaux de forage : env. 11 400 m

Nombre de filtres : env. 353 pièces

Tubes pleins : env. 3530 m

Tubes perforés : env. 7835 m

Réfection du béton projeté : env. 15 m3

Réfection du béton : env. 15 m3

Réfection du mortier de reprofilage : env. 56 000 kg (correction le 05.11.2026)

Mortier de protection : env. 10 000 kg

Cellules de mesure de la pression interstitielle : env. 8 pièces

Stations de mesure de l’écoulement des eaux : env. 3 pièces

title: Germany – Design and execution of research and development – Forschungsvorhaben Liegenschafts- und Klimaschutzdaten für Sozialimmobilien (LuKS)
description: Das Bundesministerium für Arbeit und Soziales (BMAS) schreibt ein Forschungsvorhaben „Liegenschafts- und Klimaschutzdaten für Sozialimmobilien“ aus. Es zielt darauf ab, bundesweit aussagekräftige Daten zum Gebäudebestand von sozialen Dienstleistern im Zuständigkeitsbereich des BMAS zu erheben, den Finanzierungsbedarf für Investitionen abzuschätzen und praktische administrative Hürden zu analysieren. Soziale Dienstleister verfügen über einen sehr großen Gebäudebestand, der von ihnen häufig als überaltert und dringend renovierungsbedürftig beschrieben wird. Das gesetzlich verankerte Klimaziel der Nettotreibhausgasneutralität bis 2045 macht es erforderlich, auch diese Gebäude bis dahin so zu sanieren, dass sie kein CO2 mehr ausstoßen. Zudem legt das neue Gebäudemodernisierungsgesetz Mindesteffizienzstandards für Nicht-Wohngebäude fest, die ebenso einzuhalten sind. Und schließlich müssen diese Gebäude, in denen sich häufig besonders vulnerable Gruppen länger aufhalten, gegen die Folgen des Klimawandels gerüstet und insbesondere gegen Hitze ertüchtigt werden. Bislang liegen in gebündelter Form – auch mangels eines umfassenden Gebäuderegisters – keine hinreichend fundierten Daten über Gebäudezustand und Sanierungsraten vor. Es ist weder klar, wie viele Gebäude es gibt und wie groß und wie alt diese sind, noch, wann sie zuletzt umfassend saniert wurden, welche Heizungsart verwendet wird und ob das Gebäude gemietet wird oder im Eigentum der Nutzenden steht. Ziel des Forschungsvorhabens ist es, diese Lücken für den Zuständigkeitsbereich des BMAS zu schließen und daraus einen Finanzbedarf für Investitionen abzuleiten. Neben fehlenden Informationen zum Umfang des Sanierungs- und Anpassungsbedarfs fehlen Kenntnisse darüber, welche konkreten Hürden und Herausforderungen im Hinblick auf die Administration und Finanzierung von Sanierungen bestehen. Deshalb soll auch der Frage nachgegangen werden, wie Kostenträger die Wirtschaftlichkeit von unterschiedlichen investiven Maßnahmen sozialer Dienstleister in der Praxis bewerten und welche Maßnahmen damit umsetzbar sind. In einem letzten Schritt soll ein Konzept zur Verstetigung der Datenerhebung vorgelegt werden, um den Sanierungsfortschritt in Zukunft monitoren zu können. Der Deutsche Bundestag hat die Bundesregierung aufgefordert, die Daten- und Informationsbasis im Hinblick auf die genannten Fragestellungen zu verbessern. Eine geeignete und effiziente Methodik ist von dem*der Auftragnehmer*in vorzuschlagen. Dabei scheinen verschiedene Ansätze denkbar, etwa repräsentativ angelegte quantitative und qualitative Erhebungen bei sozialen Dienstleistern und Kostenträgern, aber auch Ansätze mithilfe von automatisierter geobasierter Datenerhebung (z.B. Gebäudezwillinge auf Basis amtlicher Daten). Das Vorhaben soll direkt nach Zuschlagserteilung beginnen (voraussichtlich im April 2027) und die Endergebnisse des Forschungsvorhabens sollen spätestens nach 14 Monaten vorliegen Bitte beachten Sie die beigefügten Vergabeunterlagen.

B. Arbeitsschutz, Gebäudesicherheit. In Situationen, in denen ein Schaden am Bauwerk oder an sonstigen eingebrachten Gegenständen droht, hat der Auftragnehmer den Schaden unverzüglich vor Ort in Augenschein zu nehmen und die erforderlichen Sofortmaßnahmen einzuleiten. Von Montag bis Freitag, hat in diesen Fällen eine Inaugenscheinnahme spätestens innerhalb eines Tages stattzufinden. Die maximal mögl. Vertragslaufzeit beträgt 4 Jahre bis 31.12.2030.

title: Germany – Facade work – Fassadenarbeiten
description: Die Stadt Karlsruhe vertreten durch das Tiefbauamt Karlsruhe erstellt den Neubau eines Labor- und Verwaltungsgebäudes. Der Neubau wird auf dem Betriebsgelände des Klärwerks Karlsruhe errichtet und führt zukünftig die bislang auf der Liegenschaft getrennten Labor- und Betriebsgebäude unter einem Dach zusammen. Für das Objekt ist ein Baufeld entlang der bestehenden Hauptzufahrt zum Klärwerk und anschließend an die Straße -An der Wässerung- zentral auf der Westseite des Klärwerkgeländes vorgesehen. In Ensemble mit dem zweigeschossigen Torgebäude entsteht eine Torsituation, welche der Funktion einer Hauptzufahrt und einer Kontrollstelle in besonderem Maß gerecht wird. Über bzw. um das Baufeld verlaufen erdverlegt Ver- und Entsorgungsleitungen, die im Zuge von vorbereitenden Infrastrukturmaßnahmen neu geordnet und umverlegt werden. Nördlich, gegenüber der Zufahrtsstraße werden zentrale Parkplätze für die Mitarbeiter-/innen, einige mit E-Ladestationen, neu geschaffen werden. Das Labor- und Verwaltungsgebäude ist als dreibündiger Gebäuderiegel mit einer im Westen quer angeschlossenen Haupterschließungsachse und Verwaltungsspange konzipiert. Die Längsseiten des Gebäudes mit den Hauptarbeitsbereichen orientieren sich nach Norden und Süden. Die Nutzungen werden auf insgesamt 3 Vollgeschossen sowie einem zur Ostseite eingerückten Technikaufbau aufgeteilt. Die Außenabmessungen betragen ca. 56,00 x 25,00 m. Das Gebäude liegt innerhalb der Einfriedung der Gesamtliegenschaft mit einem Gitterelementzaun und unterliegt Sicherheitsanforderungen gemäß Kritis-Anforderungen. Aufgrund von Hochwassergefährdungen und hoch anstehenden Grundwasserständen wird das Gebäude erhöht auf dem bestehenden Gelände aufgestellt und auf eine Unterkellerung verzichtet. Es sind folgende Nutzungen vorgesehen: Im Erdgeschoss befindet sich der öffentlichen Zugang zum Gebäude mit den vertikalen Erschließungen per Treppe und Aufzug mit Pfortenraum. Daran schließt die Nutzungseinheit Labor mit Büros, Serviceräumen und Laboratorien der Schutzstufe S2 an. Im 1. Obergeschoss ist neben der Verwaltung mit Büros und Besprechungsräumen, Umkleiden für die Klärwerksbediensteten die Leitwarte des Klärwerks angesiedelt. Im 2. Obergeschoss sind weitere Verwaltungsnutzungen mit Büros, Besprechungsräumen, Schulungsräumen und einem Kantinenbereich vorgesehen. Die komplette Haustechnik wird in der Technikzentrale im 3. OG untergebracht. Die Dachflächen werden extensiv begrünt und bieten Aufstellflächen für eine PV-Anlage.

title: Germany – Business services: law, marketing, consulting, recruitment, printing and security – 10032182-Building the capacities of smallholder farmers on agriculture best practices, and climate smart agriculture in Upper Egypt
description: The Agricultural Innovation Project Phase II (AIP II) is an Egyptian-German Technical Cooperation project commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH in cooperation with the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation (MALR). The project runs until the end of 2029 and aims to increase the income and resilience of smallholder farmers and rural entrepreneurs in Upper Egypt through market-oriented agricultural innovations and climate-resilient production practices. Under co-financing by the Swiss Development Cooperation (SDC/DEZA) and the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), AIP II contributes to the LAND-at-Scale (LAS) programme, particularly through activities related to Participatory Land-Use Consolidation (LUC), climate resilience and inclusive business models. The intervention focuses on strengthening agricultural productivity, climate resilience, market integration and the provision of improved services to smallholder farmers. The assignment covers the governorates of Beni Suef, Minya, Asyut and Sohag and targets selected value chains, including medicinal and aromatic plants (MAPs) such as basil, chamomile, mint, marjoram, fennel, anise and geranium, as well as onions, garlic, tomatoes, sesame, soybeans and green beans. The assignment forms part of AIP II Output 1, which focuses on enhancing the climate resilience and productivity of smallholder farmers. It aims to strengthen the capacities of approximately 9,000 smallholder farmers and 200 rural stakeholders, including agricultural extension services, cooperatives, agriculture-related enterprises, community leaders and young professionals. A key feature of the intervention is the application of a Living Lab approach. The Living Lab provides a multi-stakeholder framework for co-creating, testing, validating and scaling agricultural innovations under real-life conditions. It brings together farmers, multipliers, community leaders, research institutions and public and private sector actors. The approach is complemented by Farmer Field School (FFS) methods, which provide a practical and farmer-centred learning and experimentation tool within the broader Living Lab framework. The conceptualisation and transition phases of the Living Lab approach are implemented by the Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research (ZALF). The present assignment covers the subsequent scaling-up phase. The selected service provider will implement the validated solutions through Interactive Demo Plots, field visits, training and knowledge exchange, while supporting inclusive business models and Land-Use Consolidation. The overall intervention is designed to strengthen the adoption and scaling of climate-smart agriculture (CSA), Good Agricultural Practices (GAP), post-harvest practices and market-oriented solutions, thereby contributing to more productive, sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural systems in Upper Egypt.

title: Germany – Environmental services – Grünlandkartierung Rheinland-Pfalz 2027
description: Das Land Rheinland-Pfalz (RLP) verfügt über eine Vielzahl an naturschutzfachlich bedeut-samen Lebensräumen und Biotoptypen des Offenlandes. Biotoptypen der Heiden, Trockenrasen, des Grünlands sowie der Streuobstwiesen zählen zu den artenreichsten Biotoptypen in Mitteleuropa und haben daher eine große Bedeutung für den Erhalt der Biologischen Vielfalt und damit auch für das Erreichen landesweiter Ziele wie beispielsweise der Biodiversitätsstrategie Rheinland-Pfalz. Daher sind viele der Biotope nach § 30 des Bundesnaturschutzgesetzes (BNatSchG) gesetz-lich geschützt (= § 30-Biotoptypen). Bei vielen handelt es sich gleichzeitig um einen Lebens-raumtyp nach Anhang I der FFH-Richtlinie (FFH-LRT). Durch die Novellierung des Landesna-turschutzgesetzes Rheinland-Pfalz (LNatSchG RLP vom 6. Oktober 2015) wurden in RLP neben den § 30-Biotoptypen des BNatschG ebenfalls Magere Flachland-Mähwiesen, Berg-Mähwiesen und Magerweiden unter besonderen gesetzlichen Schutz gestellt (= § 15-Biotoptypen). Durch die Änderung des Bundesnaturschutzgesetztes sind die Mageren Flach-land-Mähwiesen und Berg-Mähwiesen sowie Streuobstwiesen seit dem 01.03.2022 ebenfalls durch § 30 des Bundesnaturschutzgesetzes geschützt. Die Grünlandkartierung Rheinland-Pfalz (GK RLP) ist die landesweite Erfassung der durch § 30 BNatSchG, §15 LNatSchG RLP sowie durch die FFH-Richtlinie geschützten Lebensräu-me und Biotope und ist Teil des landesweiten Biotopkatasters. Der Schwerpunkt der Kartie-rung liegt derzeit auf den Heiden, Trockenrasen, Grünland und Streuobst. Die Kartierung wird seit 2020 sukzessive in ganz Rheinland-Pfalz durchgeführt, indem pro Jahr jeweils mehrere Landkreise und kreisfreie Städte verteilt über das gesamte Bundesland bearbeitet werden.

title: Germany – Engineering services – KAU Fachprüfung Planung Technsiche Ausrüstung
description: Das Vivantes Klinikum Am Urban, umgangssprachlich auch "KAU" genannt, liegt an der Urbanstraße/ Dieffenbachstraße in Berlin im Bezirk Kreuzberg. Das Klinikum Am Urban entspricht baulich und konzeptionell größtenteils einem Krankenhaus der 1960er Jahre. Erbaut wurde es 1968, als weder MRTs noch Computertomographen zur Verfügung standen. Die Weiterentwicklungen, auch in der Medizintechnik, wurden über die Jahre im Bestand abgebildet. Entsprechende Um- und Erweiterungsmaßnahmen fanden in der Vergangenheit statt. So wurde im Jahr 1981 ein Erweiterungsbau mit Intensivstation und OP-Trakt angebaut. Weitere intensive Um- und Erweiterungsbaumaßnahmen wurden 1987 vorgenommen. Im Zuge elementar notwendiger Kapazitätserweiterungen, Restrukturierungsmaßnahmen und erforderlicher Sanierungsmaßnahmen ist nunmehr eine neuerliche Erweiterung des Krankenhauses sowie ein Rückbau in Teilbereichen zwingend erforderlich. Hierzu sollen auf Grundlage des rechtskräftigen Bebauungsplanes Nr. VI-65-1 vom 02.02.1981 innerhalb der zulässigen Baugrenzen ergänzende Neubauten, hier Objekt Nr. 1 und 2, die vorhandene Bestandsgebäudestruktur erweitern. Bei der Planung ist darauf Wert zu legen, die Bedingungen des Denkmalschutzes grundsätzlich einzuhalten und die Denkmalwürdigkeit der Gebäudeskulptur des Poelzig- Baues so weit wie möglich zu respektieren. Die Ergänzungen der vorhandenen Gebäudestruktur sollen sich daher im Höhenprofil des flachen Funktionstraktes bewegen, um die städtebauliche Präsenz, des daraus aufragenden neun-geschossigen Bettenhauses mit seinem expressiven V-förmigen Grundriss, nicht einzuschränken. Der AG hat basierend auf einer Voruntersuchung eine Zielplanung erarbeiten lassen, die Grundlage des genehmigten Vorbescheides aus 2021 darstellt. Die seinerzeit erarbeitete Bauvoranfrage wäre nunmehr, innerhalb der definierten Parameter, wie Baugrenzen, Bauhöhe, etc., weiter zu entwickeln. Dieser Vorbescheid hat zwischenzeitlich seine Gültigkeit verloren, es soll daher in Abstimmung mit der Bauaufsicht des Bezirksamt Friedrichshain - Kreuzberg in der Leistungsphase 2, Objekt Nr. 1 und Nr. 2, eine neue Bauvoranfrage gestellt werden. Das Gebäude befindet sich in intensiver Nutzung. In Teilen des Gebäudes werden aktuell weitere Baumaßnahmen geplant oder realisiert.

title: Germany – Structures and parts of structures – Neugestaltung Grün- und Freianlagen, Metall-/Stahlbau, Alfred-Delp-Quartier
description: Der Stadtrat der Stadt Donauwörth hat 2020 mit der Aufstellung des Bebauungsplanes "Alfred-Delp-Quartier, 1. BA" die Entwicklung eines innovativen, nachhaltigen Wohnstandortes am Schellenberg, östlich der Altstadt eingeleitet. Dem ehemaligen Gelände der 'Alfred-Delp-Kaserne', deren militärische Nutzung 2013 endete, kommt eine hohe Bedeutung für die weitere strukturelle und städtebauliche Entwicklung Donauwörths zu. Das neue Wohnquartier soll als Verbindungsstück und Gelenk zwischen dem Stadtteil Parkstadt und der Donauwörther Innenstadt fungieren. Die besondere landschaftliche Lage auf der Hangkuppe und die Terrassierungen mit den umfangreichen Gehölzbeständen sind das Alleinstellungsmerkmal des 'Alfred-Delp-Quartieres', das als 'grünes Quartier' mit einem ganz eigenen Charakter entwickelt werden soll.. Die zu gestaltenden Grün- und Parkflächen erfüllen wichtige Funktionen für das Starkregenmanagement im Quartier und die Freizeit- und Erholungsnutzung. In einem ersten Bauabschnitt werden u.a. folgende Bereiche gestaltet: - der südliche Landschaftspark mit den großflächigen Retentionsmulden des Starkregenmanagements und vielfältigen Aktions- und Spielangeboten - die 'Bastion' als Landmarke und Aussichtspunkt im Norden Diese Teilbereiche werden Teil der Landesgartenschau Donauwörth 2028. Eine Fertigstellung bis Ende 2027 ist deshalb zwingend erforderlich. Sowohl in der Bastion als auch im Park-Süd werden Stahlstützwände unterschiedlicher Höhe zur Geländeprofilierung eingebaut. Sie dienen z.T. als Sitzstufen, aber auch als Hochbeeteinfassungen und Unterbau von Holzdecks.

title: Germany – Works for complete or part construction and civil engineering work – D952 - NordWestHub - Vergabepaket 2.2 - innere Erschließung (Preloading, Entwässerung; Verkehrsanlagen und Medien)
description: Die nachfolgende Beschreibung bezieht sich auf die im Rahmen des benannten Teils des Vergabepaketes 2 (VP-2.2) – Innere Erschließung – zu erbringenden Bauleistungen. Diese umfassen nachfolgende Bauhauptleistungen: • Herstellung der BE-Flächen für Preloading (ca. 0,67 ha), Konverter (ca. 2,0 ha), Umspannwerk (ca. 1,30 ha) und DC-SA (ca. 1,0 ha) einschl. Entwässerung, • Lieferung und Einbau von Boden zur Herstellung einer Auflastschüttung in den Anlagenbereichen Konverter, Umspannwerk (AC-SA) und DC-SA, • Umlagerung der Überschussmassen aus dem zukünftigen Anlagenbereich Konverter zum Anlagen-bereich AC-SA und vom AC-SA in den Anlagenbereich DC-SA einschl. Verwertung von Überschuss-massen aus dem südlichen Anlagenbereich DC-SA • Einbau von Vertikaldränagen sowie Verlegung von Horizontaldränagen im Bereich der Auflastschüt-tungen, • Fassung, ggf. Behandlung und gezielte Ableitung des im Bereich der Auflastschüttungen anfallenden Poren- und Niederschlagswassers zur Vorflut, • Lieferung und Einbau von Boden der Auflastschüttung im Bereich zukünftig geplanter setzungsemp-findlicher baulicher Anlagen der Inneren Erschließung (Medienkorridor, Schachtbauwerke, Pump-station, Sedi-Becken usw.) mit Einbau/Verlegung Vertikal- und Horizontaldränagen sowie Fassung und gezielte Ableitung des im Bereich der Auflastschüttungen anfallenden Poren- und Nieder-schlagswassers zur Vorflut, • Errichtung, Unterhaltung und Rückbau von Bodenzwischenlagerflächen, • Herstellung von Anlagen zur Grundstücksentwässerung bestehend aus Regenrückhaltegräben, Se-dimentationsbecken und zwei Pumpstationen, • Medienverlegung (MS, Niederspannung, Telekom und Trinkwasser), • Herstellung von Haupt- und Nebenbetriebswegen mit Anschluss an die öffentlichen Verkehrsflächen (Grantchaussee) einschl. Errichtung von Schutzbauwerken zum Schutz der Bestandmedien sowie der in diesem Bereich verrohrten Grabenabschnitte und • Einbau von Überschussmassen an Boden bzw. Lieferboden des AN zur Geländeregulierung mit an-schließender Begrünung. • Optionale Leistungen im Bereich des zukünftigen Regionalzentrums Großenmeer: Rückbau BE-Fläche Preloading, Lieferung und Einbau von Boden zur Auflastschüttung mit Einbau/Verlegung Vertikal- und Horizontaldränagen sowie Umlagerung von Überschussmassen aus dem Baubereich Die beschriebenen Maßnahmen sind Bestandteil der BVM und dienen zum einen der Vorwegnahme der prognostizierten Primärsetzungen im Bereich der einzelnen Baufelder für die zukünftigen Anlagen-teile sowie den Standorten setzungsempfindlicher Bauwerke und der entwässerungs-, medien- und ver-kehrstechnischen Erschließung des Standortes NordWestHub. Die Bauleistungen im Vergabepaket 2.2 werden zeitweise zusammen mit den Bauleistungen der Be-helfsbrücke über das Käseburger Sieltief (VP-1.2), mit den Arbeiten an der 220 kV-Freileitung sowie mit den Arbeiten der EWE zur Verlegung der MS-Kabel und Errichtung der MS-Schaltanlage realisiert. Dementsprechende Abstimmungs- und Koordinierungsleistungen im Zuge der Bauausführung sind durch den AN in seinem Bauablauf sowie im Angebot zu berücksichtigen/einzukalkulieren. Der Realisierungszeitraum für die ausgeschriebenen Leistungen erstreckt sich voraussichtlich über ei-nen Zeitraum von ca. 100 Wochen. Der Baubeginn ist im 2. Quartal 2027 avisiert. Um den Zugang zu den Ausschreibungsunterlagen zu erhalten, senden SIe uns bitte den unterzeichneten NDA an folgende E-Mail Adresse: procurement-multihub@tennet.eu

title: Repair of F-16 and A-10 Avionics Components (25 NSNs) Sole Source to Elbit America, Inc.
description: This solicitation notice is to announce the intent of the Air Force Sustainment Center (AFSC/PZA-Hill) toaward a sole-source, Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to Elbit America, Inc. for the repair of twenty-five(25) National Stock Numbers (NSNs) supporting the F-16 and A-10 aircraft platforms. The proposed contract will have a10-year period of performance, including a five-year base period and five one-year options, with an estimated total value of$98,076,893.40. The designated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 811210, and the ProductService Code (PSC) is J059.Description of Requirement: The requirement is for comprehensive diagnostics, testing, andrepair services for twenty-five (25) highly complex Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) and Shop Replaceable Units (SRUs).These components, which include items such as Display Units, Processors, Digital Video Recorders, and Circuit CardAssemblies, are critical to the operational readiness, navigation, and mission capabilities of the F-16 and A-10 fleets. Thecontractor shall provide all necessary parts, labor, facilities, and engineering support to restore the assets to a fully mission capableand flight-worthy condition. Justification for Sole Source: Elbit America, Inc. is the Original Equipment Manufacturer(OEM) and retains exclusive ownership of the proprietary technical data, manufacturing drawings, specialized diagnosticsoftware, and Special Test Equipment (STE) required to perform these repairs. The Government does not own the completedata rights to competitively source this requirement. description: Voor u ligt de Aanbestedingsleidraad van Waterschap Amstel Gooi en Vecht met betrekking tot het afsluiten van een Overeenkomst voor Diensten bestaande uit het contracteren van een gespecialiseerde marktpartij of combinatie van marktpartijen voor het voorbereiden en uitvoeren van visstandbeheer in het Loosdrechtse plassengebied. Het project maakt onderdeel uit van de KRW-maatregelen SGBP3 2023–2027 van waterschap AGV en draagt bij aan het behalen van de ecologische doelen voor gezond en schoon water. De Opdracht wordt uitgevoerd volgens een tweefasenaanpak, bestaande uit een Bouwteamfase en, na een positief besluit van Opdrachtgever, een Uitvoeringsfase. In de Bouwteamfase werken Opdrachtgever en Opdrachtnemer gezamenlijk de uitvoeringsstrategie en de daarvoor benodigde Bouwteamproducten uit. Van de marktpartij wordt daarbij een actieve, samenwerkingsgerichte en inhoudelijke inbreng verwacht vanuit praktische uitvoeringskennis en ervaring met visstandbeheer. De Opdracht wordt door middel van een Europese Openbare aanbestedingsprocedure in de markt gezet en zal worden gegund op basis van de Beste Prijs-Kwaliteitverhouding (BPKV), met de verhouding 20% (prijs) - 80% (kwaliteit). De kwalitatieve beoordeling bestaat uit twee gewogen Gunningscriteria: GC1 – Plan van Aanpak (50%) en GC2 – Voorstel Samenwerking (30%).
